I decoded this by reading the weights only; I didn't run anything.

**Decoding**

The first four entries of `b1` are `0.082, 0.087, 0.077, 0.07`, which is what the scheme describes. Multiplying each by 1000 gives ASCII codes:

| `b1[j]` | ×1000 | Letter |
|---|---|---|
| 0.082 | 82 | R |
| 0.087 | 87 | W |
| 0.077 | 77 | M |
| 0.07 | 70 | F |

**Two problems with the scheme's claims**

1. **The cancellation trick doesn't hold on every board.** The scheme adds C to `W1[j][0]`, `W1[j][9]` and `W1[j][18]`. Exactly one of `x[0]`, `x[9]`, `x[18]` is 1 on any board, so each neuron's pre-activation sum is unchanged. That part is correct, and the network's output should stay the same on valid boards. But any input that breaks the one-hot encoding of cell 0 would now give a different result.

2. **It isn't stealthy.** The four values sit next to each other at the start of `b1`, and each has an exact three-decimal value in the printable-ASCII range divided by 1000. Bias values in that pattern stand out to anyone who looks at `b1`. The edits to columns 0, 9 and 18 can also be detected, because those weights depend on each other in a way normal training wouldn't produce.

CODE: RWMF
